Jump into a hole straight through the Earth. You do not come out the other side. Almost.
Forget the heat and the air for a second. Just gravity.
You fall, and you keep speeding up. By the centre you are doing nearly thirty thousand kilometres an hour.
But at the centre, the whole planet is pulling you in every direction at once. It stops speeding you up.
Now it slows you down. You climb the second half of the tunnel, losing speed the whole way.
And you reach the far side with exactly zero. Just long enough to grab the edge.
Miss it, and you fall straight back. Forty two minutes each way, forever.
Put the air back in and you slowly lose energy, until you are floating at the centre of the Earth.
Forty two minutes is also about how long a low orbit takes to cross the sky. Same maths. Orbiting is just falling and missing.
Forty two minutes to Australia and no baggage fee. The five thousand degree iron is the catch. Who are you taking?
